title: Operational Macros Catalog and Safe Handoff Bridge
creator: Ariella Chen
description: Create a centralized catalog of operator macros (small, composable admin primitives) and a safe handoff bridge that lets first-line support execute validated macro sequences with enforced RBAC and preview/dry-run modes.
background: We have many ad-hoc admin scripts living in support docs and playbooks. Oncall contributors routinely copy/paste commands which leads to inconsistent behavior, escalations, and noisy telemetry. Recent incidents highlighted a need for smaller, composable, auditable actions that non-engineering responders can run without elevated permissions. This work complements the broader runbooks-as-tasks initiative by packaging validated actions as discrete macros with safety gates.
goals: Define a canonical macro schema and metadata for discoverability and validation
Build a catalog UI + API for listing and previewing macros
Implement an execution bridge that enforces RBAC, dry-run/preflight, and automatic telemetry tagging
Ship 12 vetted macros for common support scenarios (log-rotate, cache-prune, kv-cache-invalidate, safe-restart-service)
scope: Schema, backend API, lightweight catalog UI in Console, a secure execution proxy (bridge) with audit events, and CI validation for macros. Deliver initial macro library and operator onboarding doc.
out_of_scope: Full runbook-to-playbook transpilation, integrations with third-party ticketing for auto-remediation, and bot-driven autonomous repairs (phase 2).
success_metrics: Reduce copy/paste admin commands in support channels by 70% within 8 weeks
Decrease time-to-resolution for common incidents by 20% where macros apply
Zero high-severity security incidents caused by support-run admin actions after rollout
acceptance_criteria: Macro schema documented and reviewed (security + platform)
Catalog API endpoints implemented and reachable in staging
Console pages show catalog, details, and preview UI for each macro
Execution bridge enforces RBAC, logs events to audit stream, and supports dry-run mode
12 initial macros implemented and covered by CI lint + unit tests
End-to-end test demonstrating a dry-run and a live run with audit entry
technical_design: Macros are YAML manifests with metadata (id, name, description, inputs, preconditions, timeout, required_secrets, safe_modes). A macro executor will be a thin, authenticated service that performs input validation, substitutes inputs into parameterized templates, executes via constrained worker environments (ephemeral containers or nsjail), and emits structured audit events. The handoff bridge is an API gate that maps Linear/Support tickets to macro runs, enforces scopes via RBAC roles (support.read, support.execute.limited), and produces a preflight preview of effects by synthesizing a set of diffs when possible. All execution paths must call KMS for any credentials and respect allowlists for target clusters. Metrics and tracing will be added to the existing Ops telemetry pipeline.
implementation_steps: Draft macro manifest schema and get security/infra review
Implement macro catalog service (List/Get) and DB schema
Create Console catalog UI mockups and wire up List/Get endpoints
Build executor service with dry-run flag that validates but does not mutate
Implement bridge: auth layer, ticket-to-macro mapping, preview endpoint
Create CI validation job that lints macro manifests and runs unit tests in sandbox
Author 12 initial macros and runbook docs, add telemetry instrumentation
Canary deploy bridge and executor to staging, run simulated incidents
Roll out to production with phased access: internal eng-only, then tiered support groups
rollout_plan: Week 2-3: implement services and basic UI in staging
Week 4: onboarding docs + training session for support team
Week 5: canary with two support rotations; collect feedback and iterate
Week 6: enable for full support org with telemetry dashboards and alerts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: macros could grant excessive power. Mitigation: fine-grained RBAC, execution restrictors, mandatory peer review for macros that touch prod resources.
Risk: accidental destructive runs. Mitigation: require explicit confirmation, dry-run previews, and enforced timeouts and allowlists.
Risk: performance/latency of bridge. Mitigation: lightweight executor, caching of manifest metadata, and SLOs added to infra backlog.
Risk: secret leakage in logs. Mitigation: redact fields at ingestion, require secret references via KMS rather than inline values.
notes: Conversation with Support on 2025-02-20: they prefer a one-click preview before execution
Security requested a formal threat model and manual approval flow for macros that alter DB schemas
Plan to reuse parts of runbook-dryrun-orchestrator (reference) but keep macro manifests intentionally smaller
